images.title: Two equal sticks and a thread
images.purpose: Shows two equal sticks crossed at their midpoints, with a thread round the four ends making a rectangle with right angle corners.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two crossing sticks in the centre with a thread loop joining their four ends.
images.exact_structure: Two straight sticks of equal length, drawn as thick amber (#E69F00) bars with rounded ends, crossing at their midpoints at an angle of about 50° (not a right angle); a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot marks the crossing point. A thin teal (#0072B2) thread runs round the four stick ends in order, making a rectangle wider than it is tall, with its four corners exactly at the stick ends. A small dark square right angle mark sits inside each of the four thread corners. The label stick sits beside each stick (two times), the label thread beside the top side of the thread, and the label 90° beside the top left right angle mark. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Equal sticks crossed at their middles make a thread rectangle, so every corner is exactly 90°.
images.description: Shows two equal sticks crossed at their midpoints, with a thread round the four ends making a rectangle with right angle corners.
images.context: Equal diagonals that bisect each other at any angle give a rectangle, so each thread corner is 90°.

image_decisions.why: The doer builds 90° from two equal sticks; the simplest state of that construction is one crossing and one loop.
